chief_complaint: Pregnancy in a 43-year-old woman with chronic hypertension, CKD stage 2, and diabetes
history_of_present_illness: The patient presents with a newly documented normal pregnancy (onset 2018-09-20) while managing longstanding essential hypertension (since 2006), chronic kidney disease stage 2 (since 2013) with diabetic microalbuminuria, and prediabetes treated with insulin (likely representing overt type 2 diabetes). She also has metabolic syndrome, obesity, anemia, and chronic pain. Recent vital signs show low systolic blood pressure (92/74 mmHg) on lisinopril and amlodipine, a heart rate of 95 bpm, and an unusually low hemoglobin A1c of 3.4%, suggesting possible laboratory error or overtreatment. No prenatal labs, vitamins, or low‑dose aspirin are recorded. Social factors include low educational attainment, prior intimate‑partner violence, unemployment, and engagement in risk activities, all of which may affect adherence and outcomes.
